name: vllm_rocm_profiling_method
description: Capture, parse, and interpret vllm inference traces on ROCm. Two trace modes (cudagraph FULL_AND_PIECEWISE vs CUDAGRAPH_MODE=NONE) answer different questions; conflating them produces phantom bottlenecks. Pair with rocprof PMC counters for hardware-level diagnosis.
preconditions: vllm-rocm server with --profiler-config.profiler=torch wired (start_profile/stop_profile HTTP endpoints)
Bench client that can run a tiny workload (4-8 prompts) without overwhelming the profile
ijson available for streaming JSON parse of multi-GB trace files
Optionally rocprof/rocprofv3 for HSA-level PMC counters
steps: Choose trace mode based on the question:

- CUDAGRAPH_MODE=NONE (default cudagraph_mode=NONE in run script): every kernel launch produces a visible event with full per-kernel timing. Use for ALGORITHMIC analysis: which kernels exist, call counts, relative ordering, inter-layer sequence. WARNING: inflates per-call cost by 5-30x due to launch overhead; share percentages of sync-bound kernels (allreduce, small launches) are NOT representative of production.

- cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE (default production mode): kernels inside captured graphs still appear in trace, but per-call time reflects actual GPU runtime. Use for REAL production breakdown. Rank-0 trace sizes ~30-130 MB (cgnone gives 600+ MB).
1. Stop server, set CUDAGRAPH_MODE env (or omit for production), PROFILER_WITH_STACK=False to avoid V1 engine timeouts on TP=8.
2. Restart, wait for /v1/models endpoint to be reachable.
3. Run a brief warmup bench (absorbs any JIT compile of bind-mounted extensions).

4. curl POST /start_profile, run a small profiled bench (4 prompts conc=2 is plenty), curl POST /stop_profile. Wait for all 8 worker traces (dp0_pp0_tp{0..7}_rank{0..7}.*.pt.trace.json.gz) to flush; can take 30-60s after stop.

Parse: use ijson.items(f, 'traceEvents.item') over gzip.open(f, 'rb') to stream-parse without loading the multi-GB JSON into RAM. Filter ev.get('cat') in ('kernel', 'gpu_op') for GPU events; ev.get('cat') == 'user_annotation' for phase markers (look for 'execute_context_N(seq)_generation_M(idx)' regex, generation_0 = prefill, generation_N>0 = decode).

Bucket kernels by name with a regex/keyword classifier (allreduce_1stage, moe_gemm, mla_attn, sparse_attn_indexer, gemm_dense, quant_op, elementwise, etc.). Top 30 individual kernel names + the bucketed totals together give actionable picture.

Phase split: bisect kernel events by ts against sorted (start, end, phase) intervals from generation_N marks. In cgnone, 'unknown' bucket captures events outside marked generations (engine setup, sampler, post-process) - typically 5-15% of time.

Cross-check with rocprof PMC: rocprofv3 -i pmc.txt --pmc 'SQ_WAVES SQ_BUSY_CYCLES SQ_INSTS_VALU SQ_LDS_BANK_CONFLICT GPU_UTIL FetchSize WriteSize' -- <standalone_binary>. SQ_WAVES tells parallelism breadth (1024 SIMD slots on MI355X); SQ_BUSY_CYCLES tells per-wave work; VGPR_Count/SGPR_Count tell register pressure.

Validate suspected bottlenecks with a standalone microbench (e.g. spawn 8-process torchrun for distributed ops). Use cuda events for timing (NOT perf_counter); perf_counter under-measures GPU time when the GPU is the bottleneck because launches queue up.

Cross-check standalone vs production: the gap (often 2-3x) is REAL and explains why a microbench-winning kernel can regress in production (typically: low SQ_WAVES count gets out-scheduled when running alongside concurrent cudagraph kernels).
expected_impact: Avoids 1-2 weeks of chasing phantom bottlenecks (the 'AR is 77% of decode' trap). Pinpoints the actually-addressable kernels with first-pass accuracy.
decision_rules: If a cgnone trace shows ANY sync-bound kernel (allreduce, atomics, small launches) at >50% of decode time, recapture in cudagraph mode before believing it. cgnone inflates these 5-30x.
Per-call kernel time in cgnone trace = actual GPU compute + 5-30us launch overhead per kernel. Per-call time in cudagraph trace = actual GPU compute only.

If standalone microbench shows >1.4x win over baseline but production shows <1.1x, the standalone is hiding either L2-hot data reuse or low-occupancy launch interference. Validate with cuda events AND production cudagraph trace before believing.
torch.utils.cpp_extension.load() rebuilds when source mtime changes; cache is keyed by name. Use unique names (v1, v2, v3) when iterating on kernels to avoid stale .so reuse.

Workers in TP>1 vllm each JIT-build extensions independently; the first inference call after restart triggers compile and can timeout the request. Always do a small warmup bench between restart and the timing bench.

artifacts.pmc_counter_set: SQ_WAVES SQ_BUSY_CYCLES SQ_INSTS_VALU SQ_INSTS_LDS SQ_LDS_BANK_CONFLICT SQ_WAIT_INST_LDS GRBM_GUI_ACTIVE GPU_UTIL FetchSize WriteSize VALUBusy MemUnitStalled LDSBankConflict
